title: An Ab initio Framework for Simulating Ultrafast Nonlinear Cavity Quantum Electrodynamics Spectra
authors: Luis Vasquez, Kewei Sun, Haibo Ma, Maxim F. Gelin
abstract: In this letter we introduce a theoretical framework for the simulation of ultrafast transient absorption pump-probe spectra of molecular polaritons. We derive and implement the cavity quantum electrodynamics (QED) evolution equations of polaritonic states within the framework of the quasi-classical doorway-Window pproximation, hereto referred cQUEDA /sikeda/. This framework uses outputs from mixed quantum-classical dynamics simulations in the absence of the cavity. Then by including cavity parameters accounting for cavity rate loss, coupling strength, and frequency detuning, we simulate transient absorption pump-probe spectra. Consequently, we address one of the main standing problems of cavity QED, the simulation of polaritons ultrafast dynamics and nonlinear optical properties. We demonstrate the performance of our method by computing the ground-state bleach (GSB), stimulated emission (SE), and excited-state absorption (ESA) contributions of transient absorption pump-probe spectra of pyrazine strongly coupled to a cavity. The cQUEDA is an on-the-fly computationally efficient framework with low computer requirements: the pyrazine calculations, for example, took minutes on modern laptops. cQUEDA offers wide-ranging applicability and can be generalized to model diverse nonlinear spectroscopic signals and quantum optics responses.
summary: This paper introduces cQUEDA, a novel, computationally efficient theoretical framework for simulating ultrafast nonlinear spectroscopy in cavity QED systems. By extending the quasi-classical Doorway-Window approximation, the authors calculate the full transient absorption pump-probe spectrum, demonstrating its power by modeling pyrazine polaritons. This advances the field's ability to predict complex quantum optical responses in molecular cavities.
main_problem: The paper addresses the challenge of simulating ultrafast transient absorption pump-probe spectra of molecular polaritons, specifically tackling the simulation of polaritons' ultrafast dynamics and nonlinear optical properties in cavity Quantum Electrodynamics (QED).
main_result: The authors successfully developed and demonstrated the cQUEDA framework, showing it can compute GSB, SE, and ESA contributions to the TA PP spectra of pyrazine strongly coupled to a cavity, confirming polariton formation.
method: The method utilizes an *ab initio* framework based on the quasi-classical Doorway-Window (DW) approximation, which combines semiclassical trajectory simulations with cavity QED functions.
model_or_system: The system involves molecular polaritons formed by coupling molecular electronic states (e.g., pyrazine) to a cavity photonic mode, described by a structured Hamiltonian. The simulation framework is termed cQUEDA/sikeda.
key_observables: Transient Absorption (TA) pump-probe (PP) spectra, specifically the contributions from Ground-State Bleach (GSB), Stimulated Emission (SE), and Excited-State Absorption (ESA).
important_parameters: Cavity detuning ($\Delta\omega$), Rabi frequency ($\Omega_e$), cavity loss rate ($\kappa$), and the time delay ($T$) between pump and probe pulses.
main_assumptions: The primary approximation is that the wavepacket dynamics during the probe time ($T$) occurs without the influence of the cavity, although future work aims to relax this assumption.
figures_summary: Figure 1 shows computed TA PP signals (GSB, SE, and ESA) for pyrazine at resonance, confirming the existence of two polaritonic eigenstates and observing Rabi splitting in the SE signal.
paper_structure: The paper introduces the need for the simulation, derives the necessary Hamiltonian structure, develops the cQUEDA formalism using the DW approximation, and demonstrates its application to calculate the three spectral components (GSB, SE, ESA) for a specific molecule.
why_interesting: This work provides a computationally efficient, *ab initio* framework to model complex, nonlinear, and ultrafast dynamics in strongly coupled light-matter systems, which is a major frontier in quantum optics and AMO physics.
